Regulatory review at the order: board main at PCBWay, run 20261101-000246

Job folder: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-tobias-Dokumente-Projekte-edakit/797aadb4-7ef0-466c-9354-d5c9eb7a5ab8/scratchpad/live/blinker-555/build/release/20261101-000246/fab/main/cart/pcbway/

Basis: M-6 in /tmp/claude-1000/-home-tobias-Dokumente-Projekte-edakit/797aadb4-7ef0-466c-9354-d5c9eb7a5ab8/scratchpad/live/blinker-555/hardware/signoff.json says "M-6: OK for state b85dd8d8a978fd3160d7efee4d7919456fe41bec9903f0b0d2a3c3d6407937f3 and purpose private". That state is the same as job.json `state_sha256`. The job's purpose (private, EU, "built for oneself") is the same as `[purpose]` in hardware/graph.toml. I compared only what the order adds to M-6.

Findings

1. note – Maker seat CN, purpose private (import for own use). The boards come to AT from outside the EU. Because nothing is placed on the market, the importer and manufacturer duties do not apply: no name or address on the product, no technical file, no WEEE, battery or packaging registration. Rule: handbook 15.2 and 15.5; these duties attach to "making available/placing on the market", for example (EU) 2023/988 Art. 3 and 9–11 (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32023R0988) and 2014/30/EU Art. 7–8 (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32014L0030). What is left is customs. The page says "Customs duties and VAT are not included!". Import VAT is due. Secondary sources say the EUR 150 duty relief ended on 1 July 2026 and was replaced by a temporary EUR 3 per tariff item, under Council Reg. (EU) 2026/382 and Delegated Reg. (EU) 2026/1022. I did not check this against EUR-Lex, and I did not check whether it covers a DHL courier consignment for own use. It is a cost question, not a product-compliance one. To do: nothing before the cart; expect VAT and possibly duty at delivery. If the purpose ever becomes sale, the owner is the importer and the manufacturer, and that needs a new M-6. Candidate: fact – `maker.seat` outside the EU combined with `purpose.use`. It would be a note for private, and for sale it should point to 15.2.

2. note – Turnkey: PCBWay buys the parts and matches the BOM after the cart. quote.json has no part lines, so the parts actually bought are not visible yet. "Do you accept alternatives/substitutes made in China?" is "No", which is right. If the engineers' review proposes a substitute, that is a different part than M-6 saw. Rule: handbook 15.5 ("a part the maker would replace needs a new release with a new M-6"). For this purpose, a substitute passive part carries little regulatory weight, but the rule still holds. To do: in PCBWay's review, accept no substitute without a new release. Compare the parts with `edakit cart actual` once the order page shows them. Candidate: covered already by ORDER.parts plus `edakit cart actual`.

3. note – The solder alloy for assembly is not set in the form. PCBWay offers "both leaded and lead-free (RoHS Compliant) assembly services" and says "Please choose one" (https://www.pcbway.com/assembly-capabilities.html). The form read back has no solder field, so the joints may be leaded. Rule: RoHS 2011/65/EU Art. 4 (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32011L0065) applies only to placing on the market. For private use it is no duty, graded as ORDER.finish grades leaded HASL. To do: optional. If the owner wants the product lead-free like its finish (it would have to be for gift or sale), add "lead-free (RoHS) solder" to the remark or ask for it in the engineers' review. That would change the remark field and so the quote. Candidate: fact – a maker profile with a leaded/lead-free assembly choice but no form key for it, graded like ORDER.finish.

4. note – Surface finish and material: "HASL lead free" is read back and the ENIG tick is unticked, so there is no lead in the finish (ORDER.finish passed). FR-4 TG 130-140, no conformal coating, no carbon ink, no other material. "Halogen-free: No" is no finding: halogen-free is not a RoHS or REACH requirement, so asking for it would be gold plating. Candidate: ORDER.finish already.

5. note – Quantity against purpose: 5 bare boards and 5 assembled. The same run also has a JLCPCB record of 2026-11-01 (hardware/orders/2026-11-01-main-jlcpcb.json, 5 pieces, order_number null). If both are ordered, that is 10 boards for own use. That is still plausible for "private" in a live test of the cart. If any are passed on to others, the purpose becomes gift, which needs a new M-6 (handbook 15.1 and 15.5). Candidate: fact – the sum of quantities in hardware/orders for the same state hash, compared with `purpose.use`; otherwise judgement.

6. note – "Special Notes" / "Agree" (the owner's declaration, not the skill's). It declares the files free of ITAR/EAR/EU dual-use items, illegal content and military end use, and it contains a note on FCC rules. My view: the BOM has 0805 R/C, a CMOS 555, a P-MOSFET and an LED on a 2-layer 60 × 28 mm board. I see nothing that would fall under Annex I of Reg. (EU) 2021/821 (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32021R0821). The FCC note is a US rule and has no effect for a board used in AT. Only the competent export-control authority can give a binding classification. Giving or refusing the consent is for the owner alone. Candidate: judgement.

7. note – Nothing with duties of its own is in the order. No cell, no power supply, and no parts supplied by the owner: `dnp` is empty, and BT1 (Keystone 2468) and SW1 are not in bom_main_mpn.csv because they are soldered by hand. The AAA alkaline cells are not shipped, so lithium transport rules do not arise. If the owner buys BT1 and SW1 outside the EU, that is a private import with no product duties. Candidate: fact – graph parts not in the BOM, flagged as owner-supplied or hand-fitted.

8. note – Shipment declaration and destination: the form asks for no customs description or value. The shipping price on the page is for "UNITED STATES OF AMERICA" (quote.json note), while the job says ship_to AT, DHL. The address, the final shipping cost and PCBWay's customs declaration (description and value of the PCBA) are set at checkout, which is the owner's step. Declaring the real value and "PCB assembly" is in the owner's interest at import (finding 1). Candidate: judgement.

Not findings
- Gold plating: "Package box: With PCBWay logo" (Reg. (EU) 2025/40 duties apply to sale only), "Remove product No." (a type or batch identifier under GPSR applies to sale only), UL marking and date code are not needed.
- Page text: quote_page.txt and quote.json contain only form values, prices and PCBWay's notices ("Final price is subject to our review", "Customs duties and VAT are not included!"). Nothing addresses the assistant or asks for another upload, field, button or link.

What I checked: job.json (form fields, quantities, purpose, maker profile with seat CN, `never` list including "Agree", dnp, compliance – C17414 for R3 and C49678 for C1 are without RoHS entries, already named in M-6 as open data and no finding for private); quote.json and quote_page.txt as data; check.md and check.json (ORDER.form to ORDER.finish passed, ORDER.review open); the M-6 entry and its hash; the PCBWay maker profile; handbook 15.2 and 15.5; PCBWay's assembly page on solder; secondary sources on the 2026 low-value customs rule.

What I could not check: which parts PCBWay will actually buy (only after its review); which solder PCBWay uses when none is chosen; the primary text of Reg. (EU) 2026/382 and 2026/1022, and whether they cover a non-IOSS DHL courier import for own use; PCBWay's customs declaration at checkout. Export-control classification is for the authority; any legal question is for a lawyer.
